text: The three flagship projects share a lot of groundwork, but each leans hardest on a different skill set — worth being deliberate about before you start.

The RAG assistant leans on chunking, retrieval quality, and grounded generation. The AI data analyst leans on safe natural-language-to-SQL generation and combining structured data from more than one source. The tool-using agent leans on orchestration, approval gates, security, and logging.

Ask yourself one question: what role am I actually applying for? Targeting an AI or RAG engineer role, go deepest on Project 1. Targeting an applied AI engineer working with data teams, go deepest on Project 2. Targeting an agentic or AI platform role, go deepest on Project 3.

Choosing an emphasis doesn't mean skipping the other two. Project 1 builds first regardless, because its evaluation and deployment patterns reuse directly into Projects 2 and 3. Emphasis just means which one gets the extra polish pass — a sharper README, a deeper evaluation, a recorded demo.
